as_told.title: Life magazine withholds the Zapruder film under C.D. Jackson

plain: After Kennedy was shot in 1963, Life magazine got hold of the Zapruder film, the home movie that is the clearest footage of the killing, and is said to have put out only black and white stills with key frames missing. Michels tells it himself without naming a source. He says that "instead of releasing it in full, they only published black and white stills with certain key frames missing," and that the film was held back into the 1970s. The researcher Jeremy Riss says on another episode that the man in charge of putting the film out was Charles Douglas Jackson, known as C.D. Jackson. Riss also names a man called Gordon Gray in the same story. They raise it because, if true, one man close to these circles decided what the public saw of the assassination.
